venues.name: M&T Bank Stadium

events.enthusiasm: Purple vs burgundy under the lights — the Ravens–Commanders rivalry has real heat now. Preseason finale still draws a loud crowd; look for starters to get a series or two and the tailgates to treat it like a dress rehearsal for September.

Home opener. First real regular-season night in the building. Expect full purple, early-arriving tailgates, and the usual downtown energy that makes M&T one of the better home-field environments in the league when the Ravens are rolling.

venues.history: Ravens home since 1998. Downtown stadium with direct harbor access, Purple Friday energy, and one of the loudest regular-season crowds in the AFC North. Tailgates spill into the surrounding lots and Federal Hill bars.
venues.people_love: This is Baltimore football culture in full. The stadium sits right on the Inner Harbor, so you can walk from a pregame crab cake to the tunnel entrance. Rivalry games (especially vs the Steelers and, increasingly, the Commanders) turn the whole downtown purple. Preseason still draws real crowds because the tailgate culture never really shuts off.

venues.name: Oriole Park at Camden Yards
venues.history: Oriole Park at Camden Yards opened in 1992 and redefined the modern ballpark — brick warehouses, the B&O warehouse beyond right field, and a downtown location that put the city back in the game. Still the template every new stadium tries to copy.
venues.people_love: Best ballpark experience on the East Coast for a lot of people. You can walk from the Inner Harbor, grab a Natty Boh, and watch a game with the warehouse lights behind you. Even in a rebuild year the atmosphere stays strong — families, date nights, and the upper deck still has that classic view.

venues.name: Nationals Park
venues.history: Nationals Park opened in 2008 along the Anacostia waterfront and anchored the whole Navy Yard redevelopment. Hosted the 2018 World Series run that finally brought a title to DC.
venues.people_love: Waterfront setting, easy Metro access, and a real neighborhood now around the park. Summer nights here feel like the city finally got its baseball identity right. Good for families and for the postgame walk along the river.

venues.name: The Diamond

events.enthusiasm: Minor-league night out — cheap tickets, kids on the field, local beer, real baseball atmosphere without the big-league price.

venues.history: The Diamond has been home to the Richmond Flying Squirrels (Giants Double-A affiliate) since 2010. Classic minor-league yard with a strong local following and affordable family nights.
venues.people_love: This is the classic minor-league night out done right. Cheap tickets, kids running the bases, local beer, and a real baseball atmosphere without the big-league price. Perfect for a low-stress summer evening when you just want to be outside and watch a game.

venues.name: Lincoln Financial Field
venues.history: Lincoln Financial Field has been the Eagles' home since 2003. The Linc is known for one of the most hostile environments in the NFL when the birds are rolling — especially against the Cowboys and Giants.
venues.people_love: Philadelphia football is a lifestyle. The tailgates start early, the crowd is loud from the first series, and rivalry weeks turn the whole South Philly sports complex into a sea of green. Even when the season is rocky, the Linc still feels like an event.

venues.name: Acrisure Stadium
venues.history: Acrisure Stadium (formerly Heinz Field) sits on the North Shore with the skyline and rivers as backdrop. Steelers home since 2001 and still one of the classic cold-weather, run-the-ball venues in the league.
venues.people_love: Terrible Towels, black and gold, and a crowd that shows up in any weather. Rivalry games vs the Ravens and Browns are appointment viewing. The stadium and the surrounding North Shore make it easy to turn a game into a full day outside.

venues.name: Audi Field
venues.history: Audi Field opened 2018 in Buzzard Point.
venues.people_love: Intimate soccer atmosphere near the waterfront.
